question.question: Can a removed leader use the ReadOnlySafe singleton shortcut to emit ReadState without any post-request quorum communication when the sole installed voter is a different node?
question.importance: A read barrier issued without eligible quorum authority can undermine the library read-safety mechanism. The examined component is response eligibility, not a completed stale application read.
contexts: No communication between request and response
event_paths: Committed leader removal -> partition -> remaining voter elects and commits -> removed node ReadIndex -> local Ready.ReadStates

obligation.description: Under ReadOnlySafe, if no quorum communication occurs after a fresh ReadIndex request, local singleton support can authorize a returned ReadState only when the responder itself is the sole voter in its installed configuration. A removed node cannot count itself as the different sole voter.

scope.description: Necessary local-support eligibility for ReadOnlySafe singleton responses after applied self-removal, with optional immediate step-down disabled and zero post-request peer communication.
assumptions: Non-Byzantine peers, unique new read context, serialized RawNode methods and valid applied membership history.
No quorum acknowledgment or other network message reaches the responder after the request.
excluded: No client read completion or stale returned application value is claimed; the documented application-wait condition remains outside the endpoint.
No liveness obligation to answer a read; no response is permitted.
No claim about lease reads, general dynamic quorum histories or arbitrary reuse of contexts.

grounding.derivation: ReadOnlySafe obtains read authority by communicating with a quorum. The local singleton exception is valid because the local voter is then a quorum itself, as IsSingleton documentation assumes. MajorityConfig counts only IDs in its voter set. When the local responder is absent and no communication occurs, it has no eligible voter support for the fresh request; role state alone cannot supply it. Optional step-down changes behavior but does not weaken the separately selected ReadOnlySafe guarantee. This is a necessary support condition, not a guarantee of read completion or an equality requiring success.
grounding.applicability: Fresh request after actual applied removal, singleton voter other than responder, no network input to responder through returned Ready.
alternatives: Enabling step-down protects this history; dropping or forwarding the request without producing unsupported ReadState is permitted.
Application wait may prevent an immediate client read, but does not provide missing quorum support for this library-issued barrier.
